title.value: Catalytic Synthesis of Allenes via Isomerization of Alkynes under Phase-Transfer Catalyzed Conditions

journal.value: Journal of the American Chemical Society

abstract.value:
Catalytic isomerization of alkynes to allenes under phase-transfer catalyzed conditions is described. Commercially available quaternary ammonium salt such as tetrahexylammonium bromide acts as a very effective promoter to accelerate the reaction under mild conditions. Key words: allenes, asymmetric reactions, catalysts, isomerization, phase-transfer Phase-transfer catalysts (PTCs) are one of the most effective classes of reagents to establish a practical process because of their advantages, such as safe, mild conditions and operational simplicity.1 Although PTCs have been used in carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bond forming reactions,2,3 to the best of our knowledge, isomerization reactions promoted by PTCs have not been systematically investigated and its examples are still unknown.4 Moreover, the practical synthesis of allenyl compounds, which are useful building blocks for synthetic organic chemistry, is still an important goal.5 In order to establish the reaction system, we designed substrates 1 which include two propargylic protons. These acidic protons in 1 would be easily abstracted in basic media to be transformed into the corresponding allenes 2, as shown in Scheme 1. Synthesis of Alkynes 1 Scheme 2 At the outset, we began to examine 1a in toluene using tetrahexylammonium bromide (THAB) as a PTC. As expected, the reaction proceeded smoothly to give the desired allene 2a. Moreover this reaction was revealed to be strongly dependent on the basicity of the inorganic salts. For example, weak bases such as ${ \bf K } _ { 2 } \mathbf { C O } _ { 3 }$ or LiOH are quite ineffective even in the presence of catalyst (Table 1, entries 1 and 3). On the other hand, KOH did work as a base to afford 2a within 15 min but the reaction did not proceed without THAB even after 72 h (entries 4 and 5).7 Moreover, a catalytic amount of KOH was enough to conduct the reaction, giving 2a in good yield (entry 6). Toluene was the solvent of choice, but in diethyl ether and dichloromethane there was excellent reactivity (entries 7 and 8). Other substrates which included substituted phenyl rings were also successfully converted to the corresponding allenes (Table 2). Thus we have succeeded in the catalytic isomerization of alkynes, and we attempted the asymmetric synthesis of allenes utilizing the isomerization reaction. Using chiral quaternary ammonium salts 2a could be obtained as optically active form. After many trials, we have found that the quaternary ammonium salt $4 ^ { 8 }$ gave the best result (35% ee).
